This gives a **weak Hopf algebra** in the finite reconstruction of [Chapter 12](12-chiral-quantum-groups.md). The fusion multiplicities determine the dimensions in this example. Specifying which continuation represents an oriented half-exchange also requires the marked braiding.

terms.label: Charge measured by a current contour
terms.definition:
Apply the unweighted contour to a state prepared by a charged source. A Wilson ray in abelian Chern–Simons theory couples the gauge one-form to its integral along an oriented half-line whose endpoint lies on the boundary. Fix the boundary coordinate, a numerical current level \(k\ne0\), and a ray of charge \(a\) which is straight near the endpoint. The test contour is positively oriented and surrounds that endpoint. In the half-space calculation with a moving graph ray one requires it to remain vertical near the current tests. The source contributes the residue \(a\), shifting the zero mode of the vacuum sector. On cohomology spanned by finite angular weights the resulting state space is
\[
 \mathcal F_a=\mathbb C[p_1,p_2,\ldots]|a\rangle,\qquad
 J_{-n}=p_n,\quad J_n=kn\partial_{p_n}\ (n>0),\quad J_0=a .
\]
Here \(|a\rangle\) has no oscillator excitations, \(k\) is the \(\kappa\) of (3.8), and \((2\pi i)^{-1}\oint J(z)\,dz=J_0\).

Thus the very same double-pole relation holds for every charge. The contour distinguishes two charges which any measurement using only that pole would identify.

terms.label: Normal link complex
terms.definition:
For \(n\) distinct labelled points write \(j:\operatorname{Conf}_n(\mathbb C)\hookrightarrow\mathbb C^n\). Let \(L\) be a finite-rank complex local system in degree zero, that is, a family of vector spaces with invertible parallel transport along paths. At a boundary point \(x\), a transverse slice fixes the locations of the clusters and varies the differences inside them. The **normal link complex** \(K_x\) is the cochain complex, up to quasi-isomorphism, of the separated part of a sufficiently small transverse neighbourhood with coefficients in \(L\). Its cohomology comprises closed cochains modulo exact ones. In sheaf notation,
\[
 K_x=(Rj_*L)_x
     \simeq\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(j_!L\longrightarrow Rj_*L)\bigr)_x .
\]
Here \(Rj_*L\) takes sections and their higher cohomology on the part of each neighbourhood lying in the open. The stalk is its value in arbitrarily small neighbourhoods of \(x\). Extension by zero \(j_!L\) has zero stalk at \(x\). Taking the cone of their comparison therefore leaves precisely \(K_x\) at \(x\).

terms.label: Attaching map
terms.definition:
A local collision presents the same question before any trace is taken. Knowing the complex of fields away from the collision and the vector space at the collision still leaves the map that continues a field between them. For constructible complexes that datum can be written explicitly. Let \(i:\{x\}\hookrightarrow X\) be a closed stratum and \(j:U=X\setminus\{x\}\hookrightarrow X\) its open complement. Given a constructible complex \(L\) on \(U\) and a complex \(V\) at \(x\), an attaching morphism \(\alpha:V\to i^*Rj_*L\) determines the glued complex by the homotopy pullback
\[
Rj_*L\mathop{\times}^{h}_{i_*i^*Rj_*L} i_*V .
\]
Restriction to \(U\) recovers \(L\), and restriction to the point recovers \(V\). Restricting the projection from the glued sheaf to \(Rj_*L\) gives the chosen arrow from \(V\) to the link. For the four charge-one rays at level two, different lines in the two-dimensional degree-two cohomology of the deepest link, \(H^2(i^*Rj_*L)\), give genuinely different perverse extensions with identical stalk and costalk dimensions. For identical rays, fix the coordinate framings and specify the positive half-exchange as \(+i\). With that linearization the permutation action on \(H^2(i^*Rj_*L)\) splits as the trivial character plus the sign character. Exactly their two lines in the projective family admit this equivariance. If the coefficient is further required to be the ordinary inverse image of a sheaf on the coarse unordered space, every stabilizer must act trivially on each stalk. This singles out the quotient by the trivial line, the pullback of the downstairs middle extension. The physical theory would have to supply that last requirement or decide between the two equivariant candidates in another way. [The four-point attachment](#atlas-c-cl-05)

terms.label: Consecutive cut
terms.definition:
For the word construction, retain the external label order \(1,\ldots,n\). This orders the inputs; it imposes no real order on points of the complex curve. A monotone surjection collapses consecutive labels, and the coefficient complexes carry coherent extraordinary-pullback identifications along its diagonal map. Only adjacent repetitions disappear from a word: \((x,y,x)\) with \(x\ne y\) retains the middle insertion. A consecutive cut after the \(p\)-th input separates the blocks \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and \(\{p+1,\ldots,n\}\). Its open set is
\[
U_{p,n-p}=
\{(x_i):x_i\ne x_j\text{ whenever }i\leq p<j\}.
\tag{4.9}
\]
Collisions within either block are allowed. These are the opens used by the consecutive-cut tensor product in Chapter 5.

terms.label: Spencer complex
terms.definition:
The **Spencer complex** adjoins an exterior tangent vector \(e_i\) of degree \(-1\) at each label. Its differential contracts tangent factors with the covariant derivatives, which on the block coefficient are \(\nabla_B=\partial_{z_B}+T_B\). Denote by \(K(I)\) the total complex including the word differential. A surjection \(\alpha:I\twoheadrightarrow J\) gives a map \(K(J)\to K(I)\). It inserts the supported coefficient on the repeated labels and sends
\[
 e_j\longmapsto\sum_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i .
\]
Ordering the quotient labels by their largest preimages determines which adjacent exchanges to apply **inside each word factor**. Taking a maximum in two stages agrees with taking it once. Unitarity and Yang–Baxter identify different presentations of the same order change. The exchange hexagon and the re-rooting identity for the full principal part make these transitions chain maps. Concatenation of two words, followed by localization at all differences between their blocks, gives an associative external multiplication compatible with the support maps. The empty set carries its own scalar \(R\).

terms.label: Supported action of a bulk insertion
terms.definition:
Let \(U\subset V\times(a,b)\) with \(\varepsilon<a<b\), and let \(f\) be a bulk observable supported in \(U\). Its operation on a boundary input \(v\) is
\[
\beta_{U;V}(f)(v)=p^q\bigl(\operatorname{ext}_U(f)\, i^q(v)\bigr).
\]
The middle product is the factorization product after extension by zero. Its two factors have disjoint normal supports, which removes cross terms in the Batalin–Vilkovisky differential there. Both outside maps commute with the differentials. Thus \(\beta_{U;V}\) maps the bulk complex into the complex of continuous boundary endomorphisms, with differential \(D\mapsto dD-(-1)^{|D|}Dd\).

terms.label: Pointed Heisenberg roof
terms.definition: A roof can be evaluated explicitly. Choose a surjective state quasi-isomorphism \(p:P\to B\), a state quasi-isomorphism \(i:H\to W\) with bounded-below direct-sum energy and locally nilpotent current zero mode, and a map \(c:P\to\operatorname{Com}(W)\) into the current commutant. The commutant consists of states killed by the nonnegative modes of the current. The two commuting images give \(a(x\otimes h)=c(x)_{(-1)}i(h)\). Inverting \(i\) and \(p\otimes1\) gives \(q_B=i^{-1}a(p\otimes1)^{-1}\). On \(1\otimes h\) the map \(a\) restricts precisely to \(i\). This supplies the unit path and explains why a change of resolution must respect both legs.

terms.label: Factorized common domain
terms.definition:
The common domain is the coefficient-array intersection
\[
L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)=L_D(T)\cap N_1(T)=L_R(T)\cap N_1(T).
\]
Degree by degree, for each outer exponent \(j\), its \(s^j\)-coefficient belongs to \(T_{12}((p))\otimes M^{(j)}\) for some finite-dimensional graded subspace \(M^{(j)}\subset M_3\). The subspace may grow with \(j\), but it works for the entire inner \(p\)-series at that outer coefficient. This condition makes the intersection a dg \(Y_D\)-module and gives actual maps
\[
L_R(T)\longleftarrow L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\longrightarrow N_1(T).
\]
The construction preserves quasi-isomorphisms in each input. The outgoing action and factorwise incoming actions preserve it; a general commuting endomorphism of the joint input need not preserve finite spectator support. [The factorized common domain](#atlas-c-horizontal-factorized-common-domain).

terms.label: Upward-proper support
terms.definition: This coefficient complex has two polarizations, called \(x\) and \(p\). An internal mixed form of degree \(r\) has cohomological degree \(r-2\) in the \(x\)-polarization and \(r-1\) in the \(p\)-polarization. Put \(M=\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C_z\) and \(\overline M=(-\infty,+\infty]\times\mathbb C_z\). On each compact set of external parameters, after an external cutoff equal to one nearby, the closure of the joint coefficient support lies in one compact subset of \(M^{I_x}\times\overline M^{I_p}\), where \(I_x,I_p\) label the internal variables. Thus the \(p\)-heights share a lower bound and all complex coordinates have bounded support. Above one upper collar height for this compact set, the current is independent of each such \(p\)-height and has no differential in that height. This is the meaning of *upward-proper support* here. Particle number is finite, and these finite operations are defined over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\).

terms.label: Graph domain for Virasoro sewing
terms.definition:
A binary output \(x\) retains its positive-momentum section \(f(p)\), a meromorphic germ and, where present, a vacuum component. Let \(R_{a,b}\) be the closure of the binary outputs of labels \(a,b\) in this product. At a fixed inner position \(\zeta\), choose \(r<-\log|\zeta|\). Require that the positive section of \(x\) belong to the Banach space

\[
X_r=\{f:e^{rE(p)}f(p)\in C_0([0,\infty);\mathcal F)\cap
                         L^2(d\nu;\mathcal F)\},\qquad
\|f\|_{X_r}=\|e^{rE}f\|_\infty+\|e^{rE}f\|_2 .
\]

The domain \(D_r(R_{a,b})\) is the graph of this condition in \(R_{a,b}\times X_r\). Thus convergence controls the marked output as well as both positive norms. The measure has full support and \(f\) is continuous, so its values at each momentum are specified. This graph is complete. At the fixed position \(\zeta\), finite preparations are dense in it. For example, let \(h_*=(c-1)/24\), choose a compact ground-energy band in \((h_*,h_*+1)\) avoiding integers, and take a nonzero continuous bump \(f(p)\) supported inside it. The pure ground packet \(f(p)\Omega_p\) with its other marks zero belongs to the graph. It cannot be the output of a single original binary preparation at a fixed position, since such a preparation has a locally holomorphic ground coefficient in positive momentum.

terms.label: Mehler collar
terms.definition:
The same scalar action on a cylinder of real length \(t\) gives a two-dimensional oscillator of frequency \(n\) and mass \(n^{-2}\) in each complex coordinate. Subtract its ground energy \(n\) before removing the cutoff. The ground-state transform of its heat kernel has mean \(q^n Z_n\) and variance \(n(1-q^{2n})\), where \(q=e^{-t}\). Thus for independent unit-variance circular Gaussians \(\xi_n\),

\[
(P_qG)(Z)=\mathbb E_\xi G\!\left(
  (q^n Z_n+\sqrt{n(1-q^{2n})}\,\xi_n)_{n\ge1}\right),
 \qquad 0<q\le1 .
\]

This is the Mehler semigroup for the independent complex oscillators. It satisfies \(P_1=1\) and \(P_qP_s=P_{qs}\) by addition of the independent Gaussian noises. On the holomorphic subspace it is \(q^{L_0}\), with \(L_0=\sum_{n\ge1} nZ_n\partial_{Z_n}\) on polynomials. Indeed a monomial \(Z^{\boldsymbol m}\) has eigenvalue \(q^{\sum_n n m_n}\). The amplitude with one cylinder inserted is \(\langle F,P_qG\rangle\).

terms.label: Harmonic disk state
terms.definition: The disk Hilbert space is the closure of holomorphic polynomials in \(L^2(\mu)\). In the level-one current Fock space a creator acts by multiplication by \(p_n\), and its adjoint acts by \(n\partial_{p_n}\). The substitution \(V:p_n\mapsto Z_n\) is unitary because on both sides the distinct occupation monomials are orthogonal and \(\|Z^{\boldsymbol m}\|^2=\prod_n n^{m_n}m_n!\). A norm-one amplitude \(F\) therefore gives a probability law \(|F|^2d\mu\) on the harmonic fillings.

terms.label: Multipoint mode
terms.definition: At precision \(d\), put \(R_d=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^d)\) and \(V_d=U/\hbar^dU\), with \(U\) the divided creation algebra. An \(n\)-point mode \([f;a_1,\ldots,a_n]\) has a multiplier \(f\) regular on configurations of distinct nonzero positions and a state \(a_i\in V_d\) at each position. Integration by parts imposes \(\partial_{z_i}+T_i=0\), where \(T_i\) translates the \(i\)-th state. Concatenation multiplies the multipliers. Exchanging adjacent fields changes an ordered mode by the collision residue. At a pair \(x=y+u,y\) this residue takes the \(u^{-1}\) coefficient of \(f(y+u,y,\ldots)Y(a,u)b\). The other positions and their poles survive inside \(f\). Impose this relation at every arity. Write \(\bar M_d\) for the resulting algebra with the local vacuum \(\mathsf v=[z^{-1};\mathbf1]\) identified with the empty product \(1\).

terms.label: Cauchy lift of a matrix current
terms.definition:
Let \(e_{ij}=\ell_{ij}^{[0]}\) be the matrix-current states. The Cauchy lift of a current mode begins with the one-position mode of \(e_{ij}\). At first order its creation correction for Laurent multiplier \(f\) is

\[
-\hbar\sum_a [f(x)/(x-y);e_{ia},e_{aj}] .
\]

terms.label: Weak Hopf algebra
terms.definition:
Writing \(V_a\) for the underlying vector space of \(F(L_a)\), reconstruction gives a finite weak Hopf algebra
\[
H=\bigoplus_{a\in I}\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_a).
\]
The coproduct can be written using the tensor comparison \(J\). Let \(\pi\) project the ordinary tensor onto the relative tensor over \(B\), and let
\[
\iota(v\otimes_Bw)=\sum_i ve_i\otimes e_iw.
\]
Put \(m=J\pi\) and \(s=\iota J^{-1}\). If \(h_M\) denotes the natural action of \(h\) on \(F(M)\), then
\[
\Delta(h)_{M,N}=s_{M,N}h_{M\boxtimes N}m_{M,N},
\qquad
\varepsilon(h)=\lambda\!\left(h_{\mathbf1}\sum_i e_i\right),
\quad\lambda(e_i)=1.
\]
“Weak” refers to its unit and counit identities: the coproduct is coassociative and multiplicative, but \(\Delta(1)\) need not be \(1\otimes1\), and the scalar counit need not be multiplicative. The tensor of representations is
\[
\Delta(1)(V\otimes W),
\qquad
\Delta(1)=\sum_{i\in I}\rho_i\otimes\ell_i,
\]
where \(\rho_i,\ell_i\) are right and left actions of the idempotent \(e_i\in B\). This projection is exactly intermediate-label matching. The reconstruction preserves the ribbon structure and the finite pairing tensor. [GR7]

terms.label: Flux cocycle of a particle junction
terms.definition:
What happens if one inserts the flux twice? Write \(\mathfrak l=\mathfrak g/\mathbb C1\), and lift each polynomial Weyl symbol to its representative with zero constant term. The constant part of the commutator of two lifts is a scalar two-cocycle \(\omega\) on \(\mathfrak l\). Its class acts on the two-sided interval by cap product. Its square vanishes in algebraic cohomology at every numerical \(\hbar\ne0\), even though its four-input representative is nonzero. For example,
\[
 (\omega\wedge\omega)(x,y,x^3,y^3)=3\hbar^4 .
\]
In the Moyal formula the constant coefficient of \([x^d,y^d]\) for odd \(d\) is \(c_d=2d!(\hbar/2)^d\); mixed degrees contribute no constant. The displayed value is \(2c_1c_3\).

terms.label: Finite root jet
terms.definition:
A finite root jet in \(W_m\) is an \(R\)-linear functional on \(A_m\) vanishing above some total root degree. For example \(J_i(f)=\partial_x^i f(0)\) in charge one. Form words on the positive-charge jets, each letter \(x(w)\) in cochain degree one. Transposing the Hall merge splits a letter into two and gives the differential of this cobar algebra \(\Omega(W)\). Let \(S_R\) be the zero-differential associative algebra on \(a_i\), \(i\ge0\), in degree and charge one. Its relations are the coefficients of
\[
 (z-w+\hbar)a(z)a(w)=(w-z+\hbar)a(w)a(z),
 \qquad a(z)=\sum_{i\ge0}a_i z^i.
\]
The augmented algebra map
\[
 F_R:\Omega(W)\longrightarrow S_R,\qquad
 x(J_i)\longmapsto i!\,a_i,\qquad
 x(w)\longmapsto0\quad\text{if \(w\) has charge greater than one}
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism in every charge. The derivative at the origin is \(i!\) times the coefficient of \(x^i\). For example the charge-two boundary of \(x(J_0^2)\) maps to \(2a_0^2+\hbar(a_1a_0-a_0a_1)\), the coefficient of \(z^1w^0\) in the exchange relation. The scalar unit maps to the scalar unit.

terms.label: Translated Weil test
terms.definition:
Fixing *one* shape as the supports move leads to a test of full Riemann-hypothesis strength. Let \(b\) be the density of the infinite convolution of the uniform probability measures on \([-2^{-20-j},2^{-20-j}]\), \(j\ge1\), and put \(\phi(x)=e^x b(x)/\|e^{(\cdot)}b\|_2\). It is real, smooth and supported on \([-2^{-20},2^{-20}]\). Indeed the Fourier transform of \(b\) is the product of the corresponding sinc factors. It decays faster than any power on the real axis and has zeros only on that axis. The tilt by \(e^x\) moves those zeros away from \(|\operatorname{Im}z|\le1/2\). Set \(E_n=Q(\phi+R_{\log n}\phi)\). With \(\log^+ x=\max(0,\log x)\) for \(x>0\) and \(\log^+0=0\),
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{\log^+\max(0,-E_n)}{\log n}
       =\sup_\rho|\operatorname{Re}\rho-\tfrac12| .
\]
To prove the formula, write \(F(t)=W(\phi^**R_t\phi)\), so \(E_n=2F(0)+2F(\log n)\). Its Laplace transform has a pole at each \(\rho-\tfrac12\) since the corresponding Fourier coefficient is nonzero. Smoothness gives \(|F'(t)|\le C e^{t/2}\). The gap between successive \(\log n\) is at most \(1/n\), so lower bounds at the samples extend to the continuous function with error \(O(n^{-1/2})\). If the exponent of the sampled negative parts is below \(\eta>0\), then \(F(t)+C_\eta e^{\eta t}\) is nonnegative for sufficiently large \(C_\eta\). Its Laplace transform has no real pole to the right of \(\eta\), since \(\zeta(s)\) has no real zero in \(0<s<1\). The finite convergence abscissa of a Laplace transform of a nonnegative function is singular on the real axis. The transform therefore converges throughout \(\operatorname{Re}s>\eta\), excluding every pole there. Reflection yields one inequality in the formula, and the absolutely convergent zero expansion yields the other.

terms.label: Retained kernel
terms.definition:
A scalar field forgets its ghost output. A retained kernel keeps that output until it is paired with a coefficient functional. Let \(V=M_3^0\), let \(\mathcal G\) be the completed ghost algebra, and let \(\widehat I_L\) be its closed left ideal generated by ghost modes of index at least \(L\). Put \(F_L=\mathcal G/\widehat I_L\). A retained kernel of degree \(n\) assigns to each algebraic current state \(w\in V\) a compatible Laurent series
\[
T_L(w)\in(V\otimes F_L^n)((u)).
\]
These \(R_3\)-linear families form the retained kernel space \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}\) for \(n\ge0\); put \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}=0\) for \(n<0\). Their Laurent lower bound may depend on \(L\) and \(w\). The combined current–ghost differential \(\mathscr D\) on these kernels squares to zero. The ghost differential itself is evaluated at a larger cutoff before projection; the individual \(F_L\) are not thereby dg quotient algebras. A retained cochain has an additional state input: in degree \(j\) it belongs to
\[
\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j}
=\prod_{p\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}
\bigl(M_3^p,\mathcal E^{p+j}_{\rm ret}\bigr),
\qquad
\delta\Psi=\mathscr D\Psi-(-1)^j\Psi d_M.
\]
Thus \(\Psi(x)\) is a retained kernel on the current input \(w\), with output ghost degree \(p+j\) when \(x\in M_3^p\).

terms.label: Rooted operation
terms.definition:
A rooted operation has a distinguished input on which the coefficients act. To extend the preceding argument, keep the complete algebraic state at that input. Denote the two bulk retained kernels by \(\mathcal Y_-\) and \(\mathcal Y^\sharp\) and their exchange homotopy by \(h^\Lambda\), so that \(\delta h^\Lambda=\mathcal Y^\sharp-\mathcal Y_-\). At a fixed noncritical level the maps \(i,p,k\) contract the state complex onto the small complex while acting as the identity on its trace factor. On the small complex the prescribed pure-root kernel \(\Phi\) agrees with \(\mathcal Y_-\). The essential verification is equality as operators on arbitrary algebraic rooted states for the two trace-free generators. The trace variables are spectators in those equalities. With \(\Delta=\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp\), put
\[
K_{\rm rt}=\Delta k-h^\Lambda ip .
\]
The first term has differential \(\Delta(1-ip)\). The second has differential \((\mathcal Y_--\mathcal Y^\sharp)ip=\Delta ip\). Thus \(\delta K_{\rm rt}=\Delta\) in every rooted degree. Its scalar part vanishes because \(\Delta_0=0\) and the degree-one small states have only a trace ghost, paired with a nonnegative trace current which annihilates the rooted input. The homotopy satisfies both translation identities.

theorems.title: Ising fusion over the algebra of sectors
theorems.statement_excerpt:
How much of the tensor product of physical lines can ordinary vector spaces reproduce? In the Ising conformal field theory at central charge \(1/2\), the three simple sectors are the vacuum \(1\), a fermion \(\psi\), and the spin sector \(\sigma\). A simple sector has no proper nonzero subobject. Fusion, denoted \(\boxtimes\), combines two sectors and can split into a direct sum of possible channels. The fusion rules include
\[
\psi\boxtimes\psi=1,\qquad \psi\boxtimes\sigma=\sigma,\qquad
\sigma\boxtimes\sigma=1\oplus\psi .
\]
Suppose a faithful additive assignment to finite-dimensional complex vector spaces were to send the vacuum to \(\mathbb C\) and fusion to ordinary tensor product. The first rule would make the fermion space one-dimensional. The last would then require the spin space to have integer dimension \(d\) with \(d^2=2\).

Assigning a space to each line in a way that preserves the tensor product and unit is the purpose of a *fibre functor*. In this example a different target works. Its objects carry commuting left and right actions of an algebra and so are called bimodules. The two actions will record the two endpoint labels. For a line \(X\) with incoming simple sector \(j\) and outgoing sector \(i\), the space
\[
V_X(i,j)=\operatorname{Hom}(i,X\boxtimes j)
\]
records all such junctions. To compose two junctions one must match the internal sector. If \(A=\mathbb C^3\) and \(e_i\) is the projector onto sector \(i\), then the direct sum \(V_X=\bigoplus_{i,j}V_X(i,j)\) is an \(A\)-bimodule. Tensoring it with \(V_Y\) over \(A\) performs exactly this matching. In the ordinary vector-space tensor product the projection to the matching pairs is
\[
v\otimes w\longmapsto\sum_i ve_i\otimes e_iw .
\]
For example, given a junction \(s\to Y\boxtimes j\) and one \(i\to X\boxtimes s\), tensor the first map with \(X\) and compose to obtain \(i\to X\boxtimes(Y\boxtimes j)\). Decomposing \(Y\boxtimes j\) over all intermediate simple sectors \(s\) yields exactly \(V_{X\boxtimes Y}\). The three total dimensions are now \(3,3,4\). For instance, with \(X=\sigma\), the incoming sectors \(1,\psi,\sigma\) contribute one, one and two junctions respectively. The algebra of the three endomorphism blocks has dimension \(3^2+3^2+4^2=34\). Its tensor of modules uses the displayed projector and its unit carries all three sector labels. This gives a **weak Hopf algebra** in the finite reconstruction of [Chapter 12](12-chiral-quantum-groups.md). The fusion multiplicities determine the dimensions in this example. Specifying which continuation represents an oriented half-exchange also requires the marked braiding.

theorems.title: Proposition (ternary diagonal operations)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Proposition (ternary diagonal operations).** For ordinary right differential modules with the fully localized source and unshifted target of (4.3), the linear spans of composites through \(12|3\) and \(1|23\) have zero intersection. Consequently a strictly associative binary operation in these spaces has zero triple products.

theorems.title: Theorem: classical factorization and chiral algebras
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem: classical factorization and chiral algebras.** The above category of unital factorization algebras is equivalent to the category of unital Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebras on \(X\). The factorization sheaves acquire a canonical differential-module structure, and the corresponding right differential module is \(\omega_X\otimes B_{\{1\}}\).

theorems.title: Theorem (simultaneous cluster twists)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (simultaneous cluster twists).** Suppose the coincident points at \(x\) form nontrivial blocks \(S_1,\ldots,S_b\). A positive full twist of a block rotates all its points once around their common centre while leaving the other blocks apart. Let \(C_i\) be its action on a common fibre \(E\), using local base paths. Then
\[
 K_x\not\simeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigcap_{i=1}^b\ker(C_i-1)^{\dim E}\ne0 .
\]
Conjugating the local representation does not change the criterion. The twists commute with each other and with the angular monodromies in this local product, even when the angular monodromies fail to commute among themselves.

theorems.title: A projective line of four-ray attachments
theorems.statement_excerpt:
The link tells us which nearby classes are available. It leaves a question at the collision point itself. Which of them does a section there restrict to? Fix the labelled transverse slice \(\mathbb C^3\) and let \(i\) include its origin. To impose the middle-perversity support and cosupport bounds, one works in the abelian category of perverse sheaves. In this convention a degree-zero local system on a smooth complex threefold is shifted by \([3]\), meaning its ordinary sheaf degree is now \(-3\). Subobjects and quotients in what follows are taken in this category. Put \(V=H^2K\) and \(V'=H^3K\). For this coefficient \(P_!=j_!L[3]\) is perverse. The intermediate extension \(j_{!*}L[3]\) is the extension with no nonzero subobject or quotient on the boundary. The canonical sequence is
\[
 0\longrightarrow i_*V\longrightarrow P_!
 \longrightarrow j_{!*}L[3]\longrightarrow0 .
\]
For each line \(W\subset V\), form the quotient \(P_W=P_!/(i_*W)\) in the perverse category. Its ordinary stalk is \(i^*P_W\simeq W[1]\). The costalk \(i^!P_W\) measures local cohomology supported at the origin. Since \(i^!P_!\simeq K[2]\), the costalk sequence gives \(H^0 i^!P_W=V/W\) and \(H^1 i^!P_W=V'\), with all other groups zero.

Every line therefore gives the same ranks and the same extension off the origin. The attaching arrow \(i^*P_W\to K[3]\) on \(H^{-1}\) has image the particular line \(W\subset V\). Indeed its image is the kernel of the boundary map \(V\to H^0i^!P_W=V/W\). An isomorphism of two such sheaves acts on the separated rank-one local system by a scalar and, by naturality of \(j_!\), must carry one embedded kernel in \(P_!\) to the other. A scalar fixes each line. Hence distinct \(W\)'s give distinct isomorphism classes parametrized by \(\mathbb P(V)\cong\mathbb P^1\). This calculation concerns extensions on the fixed labelled slice. Identifying a physical collision or an oriented Hall coefficient would require its attaching morphism and compatibility with its other collision maps.

theorems.title: Theorem: connected consecutive-cut duality
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem: connected consecutive-cut duality.** In \(\mathcal W_X\), bar and cobar for consecutive-cut convolution are inverse equivalences between connected augmented coherent associative algebras and connected counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras. The equivalence includes their full mapping spaces. It requires no cohomological boundedness or finite-dimensionality of coefficients.

theorems.title: Support theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Support theorem.** Consecutive-cut duality restricts to an equivalence between factorizing coalgebras and connected algebras whose positive-arity coefficients vanish on every cut open. For a factorizing coalgebra,
\[
\overline{\Omega C}_n\simeq R\Gamma_{Z_n}(C_n)[-1].
\]
The shift is part of the formula. To see its origin, index a cube by subsets of the \(n-1\) possible cuts. A subset of size \(r-1\) gives \(r\) blocks, hence a cobar term shifted by \([-r]\). The corresponding localization cube has shift \([-(r-1)]\); the two totalizations differ by \([-1]\). Factorization identifies the entire cut cube with the localization cube, including its maps.

theorems.title: Theorem (the algebraic collision integral)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (the algebraic collision integral).** Form \(G_U(V)\) by taking an algebraic direct sum over chains of surjections, placing a chain of length \(p\) in simplicial degree \(-p\), with the usual alternating face maps on the \(K(I)\). Shuffling two chains and concatenating their coefficient words makes \(G_U(V)\) a unital dg algebra over \(R\). Its degree-zero cohomology is the intrinsic all-arity mode algebra \(\mathsf M_U(V)\).

theorems.title: Conditional unit theorem for inflated coefficients
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Conditional unit theorem for inflated coefficients.** For every simple \(\mathfrak g\) and every \(k\in\mathbb C\), under the smooth realization hypotheses of (6.1), the actual unit
\[
T\xrightarrow{\eta_T}\Psi\Phi T
\]
is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded \(H\)-complex inflated along \(q\), and therefore for every inflated \(R\)-complex. This holds with arbitrary algebraic internal support or without an internal grading.

theorems.title: Finite descent theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Finite descent theorem.** Under the split-extension, K-flatness and tensor-vanishing hypotheses above, the actual unit is invertible on every \(L\in D(B)\) if it is invertible on every unrestricted inflated \(R\)-complex.

theorems.title: Theorem (sharp tensor exponent)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (sharp tensor exponent).** The first vanishing derived tensor power of \(I\) over \(R\) is \(D+1\):
\[
 I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D}\not\simeq0,\qquad
 I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(D+1)}\simeq0
 \quad\text{in }D(R\otimes R^{\mathrm{op}}).
\]
This is an assertion about an object with its two multiplication actions. It holds in the algebraic internal grading and after forgetting that grading.

theorems.title: Conditional full-unit theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Conditional full-unit theorem.** At nonrational shifted level \(s\), in every finite-dimensional simple complex type, assume the smooth realization (6.1) with its specified right action, common Taylor cutoffs and enhanced homogeneous tensor–Hom comparison. For every ordinary unbounded \(B\)-complex \(L\) the original unit is an equivalence
\[
 \eta_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi\Phi L .
\]
This holds for the ungraded adjunction and for algebraic internal grading with arbitrary support. Algebraically, (6.4) has at most \(D+1\) inflated \(R\)-complex factors. The scalar-extension functor \(R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\) is conservative, since zero base change makes every map \(T_{j+1}(L)\to T_j(L)\) an equivalence and \(T_{D+1}(L)=0\). The affine assertion uses the additional fact that (6.1) has its unit invertible on every one of those inflated factors. The naturality squares and the finite triangles propagate precisely that unit to \(L\).

theorems.title: Smooth completeness from a common current tail
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Smooth-vector completeness is a different comparison from affine induction and from derived augmentation torsion. Put
\[
\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\qquad
\mathfrak n_L=t^L\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\qquad
F:D(\mathcal S)\longrightarrow D(\mathfrak M),
\quad G=R\operatorname{sm},
\]
where \(\mathcal S\) is the smooth positive-current module category and \(\mathfrak M\) is the category of all positive-current modules. Use algebraic integer-energy gradings, with currents lowering energy and maps preserving it. Products are taken energy by energy before the outer algebraic direct sum.

Suppose one tail annihilates all sufficiently low cohomology: there are \(L\ge1\) and an integer \(b\) such that
\[
\mathfrak n_LH^q(X)=0\qquad(q\le b).
\]
Then the actual unit is an equivalence,
\[
X\xrightarrow{\sim}GF(X)
\simeq\operatorname{holim}_n\tau^{\ge-n}X,
\]
with no bound on higher cohomology, multiplicities or energy support. For every smooth derived source \(Y\), the original map
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal S)}(Y,X)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathfrak M)}(FY,FX)
\]
is an isomorphism, including all shifts. [Common-tail completeness](#atlas-c-induction-common-tail-completeness).

theorems.title: Recognition theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Recognition theorem.** Suppose \(V\) is any unbounded dg chiral algebra over a characteristic-zero field on \(\mathbb A^1\), with a genuine closed horizontal unit. For every coherent coassociative pointing \(u:J\to C_V\), the maps \(\Theta\) and \(\Psi\) are inverse equivalences between \(\mathcal X(C_V,u)\) and \(\mathcal A_C(C_V,u)\). No homotopy from \(u\) to the genuine unit pointing is required. The equivalence is natural under all pointed coalgebra maps between these objects, including those that preserve no chosen presentation. [Arbitrary-pointing recognition](#ref-ch07-02).

theorems.title: Unitization theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Unitization theorem.** Let \(W\) be an arbitrary unbounded, possibly noncommutative and nonconstant nonunital dg chiral algebra on \(\mathbb A^1_k\). Suppose its coherent pointing \(u\) admits a strict closed horizontal degree-zero state \(a:\omega_X\to W\) such that
\[
H^0(a)=H^0(u_1):\omega_X\longrightarrow H^0(W).
\]
Then restriction along \(i\) induces equivalences on both complete character and action fibres. Consequently \(\Theta\) and \(\Psi\) are inverse for \((C_W,u)\), naturally on the full stated subcategory. The displayed equality is only in ordinary cohomology. Equality of \(a\) and \(u_1\) in full derived Hom is not a hypothesis. [Unitization from an ordinary horizontal representative](#ref-ch07-04).

theorems.title: Binary exterior-source theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Binary exterior-source theorem.** The specified comparison
\[
\rho_B:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A,B)\longrightarrow N(B)
\]
is an equivalence for every ordinary algebraic dg vertex algebra \(B\), with arbitrary translation, no commutativity assumption and no boundedness assumption. [Logarithmic quotient construction](#ref-ch07-07).

theorems.title: Theorem (finite exterior sources)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (finite exterior sources).** Let \(A_r=\Lambda(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r)\) with \(r\geq1\) finite, all generators of degree one, and differential and translation zero. In the ordinary algebraic localization above, \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A_r,X)\) is represented by the following tuples in \(X\otimes\Omega_\bullet\), for every ordinary dg vertex target \(X\). Choose the order \(1,\ldots,r\). For each nonempty subset \(I\) take two entries \(a_I,s_I\) of degrees \(2-|I|,1-|I|\), respectively, and put \(L_I=(s_I)_{(0)}\). Sum over decompositions \(I=P\sqcup Q\) into nonempty blocks with \(\max I\in Q\). Let \(\varepsilon(P,Q)\) be the sign of listing \(P\), then \(Q\), in their increasing orders. The equations are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 d a_I&=\sum_{P,Q}\varepsilon(P,Q)L_Pa_Q,\\
 d s_I&=T a_I-\sum_{P,Q}\varepsilon(P,Q)(-1)^{1-|P|}L_Ps_Q .
\end{aligned}
\]
Singletons have empty sums. For \(r=3\) the formula gives exactly the fourteen entries above, including \(c,s\). For \(X=\mathbb C\) only the \(r\) singleton companions and \(\binom r2\) pair tops can be constants of degree zero. The singleton tops give closed one-forms on the simplex. This computes
\[
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A_r,\mathbb C)
\simeq \mathbb C_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\,r+\binom r2}\times K(\mathbb C^r,1).
\]

theorems.title: The automorphism test for a genuine Heisenberg action
theorems.statement_excerpt:
There is now a description of the remaining based fibre using actual automorphisms. Form the square-zero extension
\[
X_1=H\oplus\epsilon_1H,
\qquad |\epsilon_1|=1,
\quad \epsilon_1^2=d\epsilon_1=T\epsilon_1=0,
\]
with its canonical section and projection. Work in the genuine pointed slice \(\mathcal V_{H//H}\), which retains both the under-\(H\) and over-\(H\) homotopies. Let \(U\) be the space of its automorphisms of \(X_1\) that induce the identity on state cohomology. At the trivial action \(\alpha_0\), define
\[
\Phi=\operatorname{hofib}_0
\bigl[F_{\alpha_0}\xrightarrow{\delta}K(\mathbb C,1)\bigr],
\]
where \(F_{\alpha_0}\) is the connected component of \(\alpha_0\). The scalar section makes \(\Phi\) connected, and the genuine loop comparison gives
\[
U\simeq\Omega\Phi,
\qquad
q_B\text{ is an equivalence}
\Longleftrightarrow
F^0\text{ is connected and }U\text{ is contractible}.
\]
This is an exact reduction of the original problem; neither condition on the right is established. [Genuine fibre reduction](#atlas-c-centre-genuine-heisenberg-fibre-reduction).

theorems.title: Strict three-spectator theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Strict three-spectator theorem.** For \(r=3\), every \(b_j,N_{ij}\ge0\), every positive odd \(\mu\), and every charge \(q\ge2\),
\[
H^n(D_{3,q}(b,N;\mu))=0\qquad(n<q).
\]
This holds over the whole polynomial spectator base, including simultaneous collisions, and in every homogeneity. The conclusion \(H^n=0\) for \(q\ge2\) and \(n<q\), with positive odd \(\mu\), also holds for \(r=2\) and arbitrary nonnegative \(b,N\), and for arbitrary \(r\) when every \(b_j=0\) and \(N_{ij}\ge0\). A further total theorem gives \(H^n(D_{4,5})=0\) for \(n<5\), with \(b=(1,1,1,1)\), \(\mu=1\) and arbitrary \(N_{ij}\ge0\). [Three-spectator proof](#ref-ch07-08); [four-spectator charge-five proof](#ref-ch07-09).

theorems.title: Theorem — finite radial current comparison
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — finite radial current comparison.** Assume the specified coherent smooth affine–right-\(Y\) realization, its tensor–Hom adjunction and full unit for ordinary unbounded \(Y\)-modules, its algebraic cofree model and common mode-cutoff actions. Assume also that every bounded-below smooth complex with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology belongs to the localizing category generated by \(W_K\), and that the derived ideal triangle expresses each \(Y_F\)-module by two complexes inflated from \(U_F\). Here inflation uses the augmentation \(Y_F\to U_F\), and the localizing category is closed under shifts, cones and arbitrary coproducts. Then, for every finite \(d\geq2\), every ordinary unbounded tuple \(M_1,\ldots,M_d\), and every \(X\in D_{\mathcal N}(A_K)\), the actual evaluation gives an equivalence

\[
\Xi_T(X):
R\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sm}(A_K)}
 \bigl(X,\mathcal W_K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{Y_K}S_{\mathbf a}(T)\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I_d(X;T).
\]

The comparison retains the outgoing line action, all its specified higher compatibilities, and every additional commuting incoming right action. At the regular tuple it retains all \(d\) incoming regular right actions. Its coefficient evaluations are the rational maps \(\eta_{M_1,\ldots,M_d}\) and their original affine restrictions \(b_{M_1,\ldots,M_d}\). The theorem uses the bar and scalar-extension orders stated above. See *The radial finite-puncture current recipient*, equation (45).

theorems.title: The full three-pole comparison for a finite-total spectator
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For a constant input \(T=T_{12}\otimes_{\mathbb C}M_3\), distinguish the joint intermediate object from the factorized one:
\[
E=S_w^{12}(T),\qquad
E_1=S_w(T_{12})\otimes_{\mathbb C}M_3,
\qquad c:E_1\longrightarrow E.
\]
Here \(T_{12}\) may be correlated and unbounded, and the symbol \(M_3\) denotes the third line-module input. If \(H^\bullet(M_3)\) has finite **total** dimension, \(c\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Under the chapter's retained coherent native realization and full-unit hypotheses, the full three-pole evaluation then reaches the independently factorized endpoint, preserving affine restriction and the native outgoing unit. Strict commutativity holds in the displayed algebraic bar models; smooth replacement retains the enhanced comparison and its specified coherences. A fixed left comb admits stagewise comparisons when each newly attached spectator has finite-total cohomology. Finite dimension in each degree does not suffice. [Finite-total native comparison](#atlas-c-horizontal-full-three-pole-native-finite-total).

theorems.title: Theorem (three-pole evaluation)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (three-pole evaluation).** The entire three-pole rational current resolution has an evaluation on a resolved model for \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\). The theorem holds for arbitrary constant ordinary dg inputs, in particular the regular triple \(Y^{\otimes3}\). Let \(M=T_{12}\), \(N=M_3\), \(A=Y^{\otimes2}\) and \(B=Y\). Resolve the two inputs separately by the augmented bars
\[
R_M=\operatorname{Bar}_A(A,M),\qquad R_N=\operatorname{Bar}_B(B,N).
\]
Write \(F_3(V,W)\) for the underlying array intersection just defined, with \(V\) in the completed pair and \(W\) in the spectator position. With the pair-sum twist on its free heads, \(F_3(R_M,R_N)\) augments by a quasi-isomorphism to \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\). For the evaluation target, replace the free right heads in the two bars by \(P^{\otimes2}\) and \(P\), respectively. Call the resulting bars \(T_M,T_N\). Their ordinary bar differentials give \(F_3(T_M,T_N)\) its differential.

Let \(P_c^D\) be the three-pole rational current resolution over \(D\). For \(\pi\in P_c^D\), expand \(\Delta^{(3)}(\pi)\) in the three affine heads. The direct expansion gives algebraic rational rows with common lower bounds. The factorization \(\Delta^{(3)}=(\Delta^{(12)}\otimes1)\Delta^{(12|3)}\) gives a second estimate. Each outer coefficient uses finitely many third heads, and applying the inner tensorator leaves them fixed. The two estimates put the same kernel in \(F_3(P^{\otimes2},P)\). The evaluation is the balanced chain map
\[
\begin{aligned}
\eta:P_c^D\otimes_{Y_D}F_3(R_M,R_N)&\longrightarrow F_3(T_M,T_N),\\
\pi\otimes(x\otimes y)&\longmapsto\Delta^{(3)}(\pi)\cdot(x\otimes y).
\end{aligned}
\]
The dot multiplies the heads and retains all letters and both terminal vectors, with the tensor signs. At each outer order a finite convolution of finite spectator spans suffices. The bound depends on the resolved word and the output order and permits arbitrarily long horizontal words in the incoming bars. In the chain identity the right twist of \(\Delta^{(3)}\) cancels the twist of the free heads. This explains the ordinary differential in the target.

theorems.title: Theorem (four-pole evaluation)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (four-pole evaluation).** Take constant ordinary pair inputs \(M,N\) over \(A=Y^{\otimes2}\), and write \(F_4(M,N)=L_*^{\mathrm{fac}}(M\otimes N)\). For each pair \(V=M,N\) take the bars \(R_V=\operatorname{Bar}_A(A,V)\) and \(T_V=\operatorname{Bar}_A(P^{\otimes2},V)\). Over \(D_*\), the four-pole resolution \(P_{c,*}^{(4)}\) has the evaluation
\[
P_{c,*}^{(4)}\otimes_{Y_{D_*}}F_4(R_M,R_N)\longrightarrow F_4(T_M,T_N),
\qquad \pi\otimes b\longmapsto\Delta^{(4)}(\pi)\cdot b .
\]
The source bars carry the four-point interaction and the target bars their ordinary bar differential. To see why the source resolves the stated intersection, contract an acyclic first input over \(\mathbb C\). Perturb its contraction first by the internal \(12\) kernel. A term of order \(e\) contributes \(q^e s_1^{-e}\) on the radial side and \(p_1^e\) in the first completed pair. It respects the conic bound and acts only in that pair. Next perturb by the four cross-pair kernels. All have positive outer order with finitely many factorwise operators in each coefficient. The resulting series converges on both sides and preserves finite tensor rank there. Interchanging the pairs proves invariance under a quasi-isomorphism in either input.

Write \(P_{c,*}^{(4)}\) for the four-pole resolution extended from distinct positions to \(D_*\). For \(\pi\) in this resolution the direct \(\Delta^{(4)}(\pi)\) satisfies the conic estimate. Its factorization
\[
\Delta^{(4)}=(\Delta^{(12)}\otimes\Delta^{(34)})\Delta^{(12|34)}
\]
has finitely many tensors of rational pair heads at each \(q\)-coefficient. Each inner tensorator acts only on its own head. Thus multiplying the independent free bar heads by this kernel lands in the same intersection with two affine heads in each target bar. The radial shuffle respects the multiplication. The comparison with the outer binary evaluation uses the two rational pair heads before applying their respective inner tensorators. Both sides carry the same right actions, affine restriction and unit normalization on the resolved words. The construction supplies a map on all the stated coefficients, including the regular inputs, without a finite-total cohomology hypothesis. [Four-pole rational tensorator](#atlas-c-horizontal-four-pole-rational-tensorator).

theorems.title: Theorem — finite marked Ward calculus
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — finite marked Ward calculus.** With the stated compatible flats, internal gates, finite pole and jet orders, upward-proper coefficient support and canonical scalar extension, \(\mathcal D\mathcal M_I\subseteq\mathcal M_I\). For a scalar coefficient \(K\) with \(q\) marked factors, its derivative consists of four finite sums:

\[
DK=\mathcal B(K)+\mathcal S(K)+\mathcal V(K)+\mathcal C(K).
\]

Here \(\mathcal B\) replaces a ray by an additional mark with sign \((-1)^q\); \(\mathcal S\) takes the residues of entire complex-parallel scalar classes; \(\mathcal V\) takes the oriented real boundaries of whole simplified gates; and \(\mathcal C\) is the sum over closed critical marked flats. Its coefficients are the annular moments of the whole weighted, gated normal kernel. The derivative of \(KF\) also includes \((-1)^qK\mathcal DF\). Old normal degrees contribute their Koszul sign, and every residue differentiates the entire remaining coefficient and field family to the required finite normal order.

theorems.title: Theorem — radial circuit transport
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — radial circuit transport.** On the actual span \(\mathscr S\) of the complete first and successive circuit contacts, their stated spectator compositions, smooth form multiples and finite holomorphic derivatives, the positive-scale pullback has a unique continuous joint-current extension to zero. It extends as a chain family to
\(\mathscr V=\mathscr S+d_F\mathscr S\). Its proper parameter integral gives

\[
H_F(\alpha,\gamma)=(h\alpha,-h\gamma),\qquad
h=\int_0^1\iota_{\partial_\lambda}\mathcal P\,d\lambda,
\]

\[
d_FH_F+H_Fd_F=\operatorname{id}-\operatorname{sp}_0.
\]

Both endpoints and the homotopy take values in the original ambient relative current complex with the same \(Z\). The three successive contact branches retain their full sum-zero relation, including unmatched fields, vacuum terms and all finite normal jets.

theorems.title: Theorem (transport of the two-mark contact)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (transport of the two-mark contact).** Adjoin \(U\), its smooth multiples, finite holomorphic derivatives and full \(d_F\)-descendants to \(\mathscr V\). The continuous cylinder limit on this larger space respects relations of joint currents because it is the ordinary pullback at every positive \(\lambda\). Applying Stokes on \([\epsilon,1]\) and passing to the limit recovers \(d_FH_F+H_Fd_F=1-\operatorname{sp}_0\) in the same fixed relative recipient. Any further disjoint spectator made solely of \(W\)'s and their finite holomorphic jets can be appended to this sector. Its only possible contractions would need an unmatched \(J\), so the next native product simply adjoins and symmetrizes the coefficient particles.

theorems.title: Theorem 10.1 (finite analytic sewing)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 10.1 (finite analytic sewing).** Under the normalized boundary hypothesis and the two-radius estimates above, fix \(d\ge2\), \(s\in\mathbb R\), positive external labels, and

\[
K\Subset\{0<|a_2|<\cdots<|a_d|,\;
                              s<-\log|a_d|\}
\]

on a logarithmic coordinate cover. There is a finite input exponent \(t_K\) for which the actual left-associated sewing is a holomorphic Hilbert–Schmidt family

\[
C_d(\mathbf a):
\widehat\bigotimes_{i=1}^{d}{}_{\!2}H_{p_i}[t_K]
                         \longrightarrow\mathcal Z_d[s].
\]

It therefore acts continuously on \(E_{\mathbf p}\). Every internal and output spectrum and every descendant level is uncut. Finite cutoffs converge normally in this operator norm on smaller compact sets. The scalar factor is exactly

\[
2^{(d-1)/4}\sqrt{\prod_{v}C_0(k_{v,L},k_{v,R},k_v)},
\]

with one factor for each binary vertex. Bounds are uniform in the external positive labels and locally uniform in \(c\). They need not be uniform in \(d\), near collisions, or at the boundary of the strict output inequality. [*Radial comb sewings*, Theorem FC.3](#ref-ch10-01).

theorems.title: Theorem 10.2 (intrinsic complete sources)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 10.2 (intrinsic complete sources).** With these elementary spaces, their original topologies and the analytic hypotheses already stated, \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(R)\) is complete and Hausdorff and injects continuously and densely into \(R\). Every continuous Virasoro map restricts continuously to these sources. Meromorphic vector-field germs with finite principal part act by absolutely convergent mode series. On the elementary positive and vacuum objects the construction recovers the original topology exactly; in particular,

\[
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(R_p)
 =\mathscr E_p,
\qquad
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(V(M))
 =M\widehat\otimes_\pi G.
\]

An arbitrary common source need not be metrizable or nuclear. [*Complete functorial sources extending the original inputs*, Theorems IS.1–IS.4](#ref-ch10-08).

theorems.title: Two independently completed conformal blocks
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Put the outer separation equal to one. For \(s<0\), take \(r>\log 2\) and \(t>\log 2\) sufficiently large on the moving leg for the two-radius estimate. Take two independent inputs on the corresponding graphs with positive sections \(f(p),g(q)\). Under the normalized boundary hypothesis the two continuous outputs on their completed projective tensor product are

\[
\begin{aligned}
 (p,q,e)&\longmapsto\mu_{p,q}(1)(f(p),g(q))(e)
   &&\text{in }L^2(d\nu(p)d\nu(q)d\nu(e);H_e[s]),\\
 p&\longmapsto\beta_{p,p}(1)(f(p),g(p))
   &&\text{in }V(L^2(d\nu)).
\end{aligned}
\]

Here \(\beta_{p,p}\) is the bilinear three-point vacuum block with value one on its three highest vectors. The first map integrates the Gaussian bound of the positive kernel. The second keeps the common momentum as an output variable. Against \(d\nu(p)d\nu(q)\) its diagonal has density \(\delta(p-q)/m_{\mathfrak b}(q)\). The annular estimate bounds its resolved Hilbert norm by \(C\|e^{rE}f\|_\infty\|e^{tE}g\|_2\). For two ground packets this vacuum coefficient is the function \(f(p)g(p)\). Shrinking both packets to width \(\varepsilon\) and taking their height to be \(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\) keeps their separate Hilbert norms bounded, but the \(L^2\) norm of the product grows as \(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\). The supremum norm in \(X_r\) controls precisely this concentration. Integrating the common momentum away would lose the test.

theorems.title: A mixed measurement separates states with identical mode marginals
theorems.statement_excerpt:
On the half-space take the closed cycles \(i_\hbar I_B((p_1^2\pm p_2)/2)\). On the disk take the two amplitudes \(F_\pm=(Z_1^2\pm Z_2)/2\) and measure the real, rotation-invariant function of the central field derivatives

\[
C=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(h'(0)^2\overline{h''(0)}\bigr)
  =Z_1^2\bar Z_2+\bar Z_1^2Z_2 .
\]

Its operator on holomorphic states is the Toeplitz operator \(T_C\), multiplication by \(C\) followed by orthogonal projection. Gaussian integration by parts turns \(\bar Z_n\) under this projection into \(n\partial_{Z_n}\). The two indices in each term are distinct, so \(T_C=VOV^{-1}\) on polynomials. The vectors \(p_1^2,p_2\) are orthogonal, each has squared norm two, and \(O\) exchanges them with coefficient two. Both states have norm one. Under the unitary \(V\) the Fock-space calculation gives \(\langle F_\pm,T_CF_\pm\rangle=\pm2\).

The disk probabilities give a direct check of what is measured. Put \(x=Z_1=h'(0)\) and \(y=Z_2=h''(0)\). Under the vacuum law \(\mu\) these are independent circular complex Gaussians with \(\mathbb E_\mu|x|^2=1\) and \(\mathbb E_\mu|y|^2=2\). The two preparations have densities relative to \(\mu\)
\[
 |F_\pm|^2=\tfrac14|x^2\pm y|^2
 =\tfrac14(|x|^4+|y|^2)\ \pm\ \tfrac12\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y).
\]
Their difference is \(R=\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y)\). It integrates to zero at fixed \(x\) by the circular symmetry of \(y\), and at fixed \(y\) by that of \(x\). Thus the two marginal distributions agree for each mode. To test the joint distribution, observe that \(x^2\bar y\) is circular and \(\mathbb E_\mu|x|^4=2\). Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu R^2=\tfrac12\mathbb E_\mu|x|^4\,\mathbb E_\mu|y|^2=2.
\]
The term \(R(|x|^4+|y|^2)\) has zero expectation by symmetry. The joint observable \(C=2R\) therefore has mean \(+2\) in \(|F_+|^2d\mu\) and \(-2\) in \(|F_-|^2d\mu\). A single measurement gives the value \(2\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y)\) for that filling, which varies with both boundary modes.

Both amplitudes have energy two. The **one-sided** collar pairing and its normalization are consequently

\[
\langle F_\pm,P_qT_CF_\pm\rangle=\pm2q^2,\qquad
\langle F_\pm,P_qF_\pm\rangle=q^2 .
\]

theorems.title: A neutral level-one ray pair and a sourced disk at finite radius
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Each of the first \(N\) means shifts to \(ar^n\) and its variance remains \(n\). For \(M\le N\), the disk inner product of \(e^{ah_M(r)}\) and \(e^{ah_N(r)}\) is \(e^{a^2L_M}\), by independence of the tail. The squared distance is therefore \(e^{a^2L_N}-e^{a^2L_M}\). The exponentials converge in the holomorphic Hilbert space, and their normalized squared moduli converge in \(L^1(\mu)\). The ray state has squared norm \(r^{-2a^2}(1-r^2)^{-a^2}\). Its normalized harmonic filling law is exactly \(e^{2a\operatorname{Re}h(r)-a^2L}\,d\mu\).

On the second holomorphic amplitude the real collar replaces \(r\) by \(qr\). Pairing with the first inserts \(qr^2\) into the covariance sum. With \(V\) the Fock-to-disk isometry, this gives

\[
\frac{\langle V\Psi_{a,r},P_q V\Psi_{a,r}\rangle}
     {\|V\Psi_{a,r}\|^2}
=\exp\!\left(a^2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(q^n-1)r^{2n}}{n}\right)
=\left(\frac{1-r^2}{1-qr^2}\right)^{a^2}.
\]

This pairing equals one when the collar length is zero or the charge vanishes. For nonzero real \(a\) the unnormalized norm diverges as \(r\uparrow1\). Neutrality places the output in the disk theory with its constant mode fixed to zero. A nonneutral output requires a charged zero-mode sector. Absolute cap normalization would also have to retain the three-dimensional mutual scalar, which cancels from the probability law.

theorems.title: Theorem 11.1 (normalized numerical Gaussian)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 11.1 (normalized numerical Gaussian).** Fix the original metric and density, \(0<|q|<1\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), and a smooth integrable \(\mu\) with zero normal trace in the single small \(C^1\) inverse neighbourhood. Supply a smooth solution \(T_\mu\) of the Ward equation above, based by \(T_0=0\) for families through zero. Couple the normalized even finite-cycle integrals using the same singular-pair Gaussian coordinates at every window. The resulting fields \(\Phi_{\Lambda,\mu}\) converge in mean square and almost surely in \(\mathscr D_{-6}\) to a centered Radon Gaussian \(\Phi_\mu\). Its law has support equal to the closure of \(\mathfrak A_\mu\mathsf W\). For a real orthonormal basis \(e_n\) of \(\mathsf W\),

\[
\mathbb E\|\Phi_\mu-\Phi_{\Lambda,\mu}\|_{-6}^2
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
 \sum_{e_n\notin\Lambda}\|\mathfrak A_\mu e_n\|_{-6}^2
\longrightarrow0.
\]

The real covariance is
\(\frac{\hbar}{2}\mathfrak A_\mu\mathfrak A_\mu^*\), with the real Hilbert adjoint. Odd and mixed moments converge by the graded Wick rule for the full inverse action. They do not define an odd-variable probability measure. Parameter-uniform statements require bounds on the finitely many higher source and background seminorms used in the estimates. [*A numerical Gaussian on the native source graph*, Theorems 4–6](#ref-ch11-01).

theorems.title: Theorem 11.2 (original heat finite part)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 11.2 (original heat finite part).** Use the original fixed-adjoint weighted realization above, with smooth reflected \(\mu,T\) sufficiently small in \(\|\mu\|_{C^4}+\|T\|_{C^1}\) and the stated bounds on higher seminorms. Put \(\ell_q=-\log|q|\). The coefficient supertrace on the reflection-even sector has, for every \(0<\delta<1/2\),

\[
\tau_+(t,u)=\operatorname{Str}_{X}(Ne^{-tA_+(u)})
=-\frac{\ell_q}{4t}+\frac{B(u)}{\sqrt t}+C(u)+O(t^\delta),
\]

where \(B(u),C(u)\) are scalar local heat coefficients. The estimate holds after each specified finite number of source derivatives under the higher-seminorm bounds. The coefficient of \(t^0\log t\) is zero. Consequently, with

\[
W_\epsilon(u)=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\tau_+(t,u)\frac{dt}{t},
\qquad
D_\epsilon(u)=\frac{\ell_q}{4\epsilon}
 -\frac{2B(u)}{\sqrt\epsilon}+C(u)\log\epsilon,
\]

the finite part \(W_{\mathrm{fp}}=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}(W_\epsilon-D_\epsilon)\) exists with error \(O_{C^k}(\epsilon^\delta)\). It is holomorphic on the admitted holomorphic source families. [*The original coefficient heat finite part and its based vacuum line*, Theorems 3–4](#ref-ch11-04).

theorems.title: Theorem (spectral field and coproduct construction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (spectral field and coproduct construction).** Under the hypotheses above, \(V_\eta\) is a quantum vertex algebra with vacuum \(1\), translation \(T\), and rational exchange
\[
\mathcal S_\eta(z)(a\otimes b)
=a_{(0)}\otimes b_{(0)}\rho_z(a_{(1)},b_{(1)}).
\]
Every finite ordered product on a fixed state has a common finite denominator. For \(V_1=V_{\eta_1}\) and \(V_2=V_{\eta_2}\), their tensor product \(\boxtimes_\rho\) has underlying module \(V_1\otimes_RV_2\) and fields
\[
Y_{12}(a\otimes b,z)(c\otimes d)
=Y_1(a,z)c_{(0)}\otimes Y_2(b_{(0)},z)d\,
\rho_{-z}(c_{(1)},b_{(1)}).
\]
The maps
\[
D_{\eta_1,\eta_2}=(\eta_2\otimes1)\Delta:
V_{\eta_1\eta_2}\longrightarrow
V_{\eta_1}\boxtimes_\rho V_{\eta_2}
\]
preserve fields, vacuum, translation and coaction. They are coassociative, with counit \(\varepsilon:V_{\mathrm{id}}\to R\) at the identity level. They induce maps of residue coalgebras and their augmented associative chiral cobars. Over a field, the same constructions descend to the ordered collision schemes. [CQ2]

theorems.title: Spin intertwiners and the oriented Ising half-turn
theorems.statement_excerpt:
There are two paths for fusing three spins to one spin, according as the first pair gives the vacuum or the fermion. In the real trivalent basis, with \(\zeta=e^{\pi i/8}\), the positive half-turn of the first pair and the change of fusion channel have matrices

\[
B_1=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{-1}&0\\0&\zeta^3\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Removing the scalar \(\zeta^{-2}\) from \(B_1^2\) gives \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\). For the second pair it gives \(FZF=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The two involutions anticommute and their products span the full two-by-two matrix algebra. More generally the complex algebra generated by adjacent double exchanges on \(\sigma^{\boxtimes n}\) is its entire intertwiner algebra. For instance four spins have two vacuum paths and two fermion paths, giving \(M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus M_2(\mathbb C)\). This assertion takes linear combinations of braids. In each simple output of multiplicity \(d\), individual pure braids have only \(d^2\) projective images.

Reflection inverts both half-turn phases. Their **labelled ratio** in the fermion and vacuum channels changes from \(i\) to \(-i\), while both squared phases acquire the same factor \(i\). Thus projective double exchanges lose the orientation. The twist of a framed spin, \(\zeta\) in the given orientation and \(\zeta^{-1}\) in the mirror, also distinguishes them. For the Gaussian rays of Chapter 11 the variance of the comparison matters even in a one-dimensional channel. At level \(k\ne0\) the operation on charges \(a,b\) has coefficient \(z^{ab/k}\), with upper half-turn \(e^{\pi iab/k}\). Parallel transport on the dual state line has the inverse phase. Evaluation pairs the two transports to one. [CQ9, CQ10]

theorems.title: Theorem (rational affine field comparison)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (rational affine field comparison).** For every \(N\ge2\) and every \(K\in\mathbb C\), the divided determinant-one double is topologically free over \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\). Multiplication identifies it, as a module, with the \(\hbar\)-adically completed tensor product of its creation and annihilation halves. The integral divided-state fields agree with the Etingof–Kazhdan quantum affine fields on every state and on their exchange. Their classical determinant-one fibre is \(V_K(\mathfrak{sl}_N)\), with the trace-form normalization. [CQ4]

theorems.title: The rank-two determinant-one RTT double in normalized modes modulo \(\hbar^2\)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
The negative-current lift also includes the shift of its argument by \(-K\hbar/2\). With these prescribed lifts, at rank two and **every** numerical level \(K\) there is an injective algebra homomorphism with proper image

\[
D_K/\hbar^2D_K\ \longrightarrow\ \bar M_2 .
\]

The precision is taken **after division** of the two same-half RTT relations and the centered mixed relation by \(\hbar^2\), and of each determinant defect by \(\hbar\). Thus the identities retain the constant and linear coefficients of each divided relation. Both divided determinants hold to this precision in every rank \(N\ge2\), even before identifying the local vacuum. For the determinant, the descending-column shifts give a translation of the diagonal states, which cancels their first integral trace correction. The remaining coefficient is an exchange difference whose collision residue is the ordered state product. In the mixed rank-two relation, sliding a current across both slots of its Cauchy correction keeps the spectator pole. The derivative from undoing the spectral shift cancels the central first-order correction. These computations take place inside the mode algebra. [CQ11]

theorems.title: Torsion lengths in the exceptional universal \(W_4\) vacuum complex
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_4\), write \(\tau=k+4\). At
\[
\tau=\frac32,-\frac32,\frac23,-\frac23,
\]
the dimensions in degrees zero through fifteen are
\[
(1,0,0,1,0,1,0,1,2,1,1,1,2,0,0,1),
\]
and all higher groups vanish. The total dimension is twelve, whereas the generic exterior algebra on degrees \(3,5,7\) has dimension eight. The primitive products satisfy
\[
\eta_3\eta_5\ne0,\qquad
\eta_3\eta_7\ne0,\qquad
\eta_5\eta_7=0.
\]
Exactly two local torsion pairs, in degrees \((8,9)\) and \((11,12)\), account for the excess. To see what specialization detects, consider a two-term summand \(R\xrightarrow{\,t^\ell\,}R\) over a local parameter ring, with \(\ell\ge1\). Its differential is invertible after \(t\) is inverted and zero after \(t=0\). All positive \(\ell\) give the same two special-fibre dimensions. Lifting the lower generator, applying the differential, dividing by \(t\) and reducing again gives a nonzero map precisely for \(\ell=1\). This is the first Bockstein on that summand. In the local parameter \(t=\tau-\tau_0\), write the finite zero-weight differential as \(A+tB+O(t^2)\). On a class killed by \(A\), reduction of \(B\) modulo the image of \(A\) is the first Bockstein. In each of the two degrees its rank is one at both \(\tau_0=3/2\) and \(-3/2\). Indeed null vectors on opposite sides of the constant matrix have nonzero pairing through \(B\), detected modulo \(1000003\) on maximal-rank minors. A single nonunit elementary divisor occurs in each degree, so it has valuation one. The reciprocal parameter change takes a uniformizer to a unit times a uniformizer. Thus both torsion summands are \(R/(t)\) at each of the four points, for \(R=\mathbb C[\tau]_{(\tau-\tau_0)}\). [CQ8, CQ12]

theorems.title: Theorem (ordinary classical reconstruction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (ordinary classical reconstruction).** Fix an ordinary unital Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebra \(A\) on a smooth separated complex algebraic curve \(X\). For arbitrary classical parameter schemes \(T\to X^I\), its complete ordinary coefficient-family categories form a quasi-coherent-linear unital weak factorization system. They have categorical base change, coherent collision equivalences for every surjection, unit insertions, separated external fusion, and compatible evaluation on the minimal coefficient. The empty category is \(\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}\), and its inserted vacuum realizes \(\operatorname{Fact}(A)\), including the normalized empty algebra and all collision extensions. Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Rec}\bigl(\mathcal C(A),F\bigr)\cong A.
\]
All tensors are ordinary. Category tensors are taken among locally presentable complex-linear categories and cocontinuous functors; descent is Zariski. No flatness or finite-generation condition is imposed on action coefficient modules, and parameter schemes may be nonreduced or have coincident marked sections. [GR1, Theorem 9.1]

theorems.title: Theorem (supported Vandermonde pro-duality)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (supported Vandermonde pro-duality).** For every finite position set \(I\) and every state count \(n\),
\[
\Phi_{I,n}=V_n^\sharp:
(\mathcal C^+_{I,n})^\sharp
\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal C^-_{I,n})^\sharp
\]
is an isomorphism of the full supported pro-diagrams and their dual vacuum triangles. It retains all finite normal derivatives and the spectator extension at three positions, and commutes with finite-stage numerical specialization of \(\kappa\). Its cut products are intertwined by the cross Vandermonde factors. [GR4]

theorems.title: The weak Hopf algebra of Ising sectors
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For the Ising model \((p,q)=(3,4)\), the simples \(1,\psi,\sigma\) satisfy
\[
\psi^2=1,\qquad\psi\sigma=\sigma,\qquad
\sigma^2=1+\psi.
\]
A faithful additive tensor functor to finite vector spaces with scalar unit would give positive integer dimensions with
\[
d_\psi^2=1,\qquad d_\sigma^2=1+d_\psi=2,
\]
which is impossible. The finite-base functor has no such problem. Its \(\sigma\)-bimodule has component dimensions
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&1\\
0&0&1\\
1&1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the ordinary vector dimensions of \(F(1),F(\psi),F(\sigma)\) are \(3,3,4\). Consequently
\[
H\cong\operatorname{Mat}_3(\mathbb C)
\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_3(\mathbb C)
\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_4(\mathbb C),
\qquad\dim H=34.
\]
The tensor projection on \(V_\sigma\otimes V_\sigma\) has rank six, matching the two three-dimensional summands of \(F(1\oplus\psi)\). A sixteen-dimensional ordinary tensor product would have forgotten the intermediate labels.

theorems.title: Theorem: the flux class in derived particle composition
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: the flux class in derived particle composition.** For every integer \(N\ge1\) and every numerical \(\hbar\ne0\), \(\phi_N\) is surjective. Its kernel \(I_N\) is generated by the Newton relation \(e_{N+1}\), the elementary symmetric polynomial expressed in the power sums \(J(x^k)\), and \(I_N^2=I_N\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0.
\]
To identify a degree-two contribution, quotient the Weyl Lie algebra by its scalar centre. Two lifts of elements of this quotient can have a scalar commutator even when their classes commute; for instance \([x,y]=\hbar 1\). This scalar defect defines the class of the central extension
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathbb C1\longrightarrow\mathfrak g
\longrightarrow\mathfrak g/\mathbb C1\longrightarrow0
\]
and will be denoted by \(\omega\). Capping a degree-two sewing class with \(\omega\) evaluates it on that extension and gives a split surjection of \(A_N\)-bimodules
\[
\omega\mathbin{\frown}-:
\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\twoheadrightarrow A_N.
\]
Every sewing Tor group is a possibly infinite direct sum of the bimodules
\[
D(\tau)=(\tau\otimes W_\hbar^{\otimes N})^{S_N},
\]
where \(\tau\) runs through irreducible representations of \(S_N\). These modules are projective separately on the left and on the right. The cap kernel is canonically \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U(\mathfrak g)}_2(A_N,A_N)\), while its splitting requires a choice. At \(N=1\), the cap is an isomorphism; for \(N\ge2\), the kernel's multiplicities remain to be determined. See [*The junction with its flux class*, Theorems 4–6](#ref-ch14-01).

theorems.title: A vanishing flux square and its locality obstruction
theorems.statement_excerpt:
What happens if one inserts the flux twice? Write \(\mathfrak l=\mathfrak g/\mathbb C1\), and lift each polynomial Weyl symbol to its representative with zero constant term. The constant part of the commutator of two lifts is a scalar two-cocycle \(\omega\) on \(\mathfrak l\). Its class acts on the two-sided interval by cap product. Its square vanishes in algebraic cohomology at every numerical \(\hbar\ne0\), even though its four-input representative is nonzero. For example,
\[
 (\omega\wedge\omega)(x,y,x^3,y^3)=3\hbar^4 .
\]
In the Moyal formula the constant coefficient of \([x^d,y^d]\) for odd \(d\) is \(c_d=2d!(\hbar/2)^d\); mixed degrees contribute no constant. The displayed value is \(2c_1c_3\).

The primitive comes from cyclic homology of the polynomial Weyl algebra. The normalized Hochschild chain \(u=\hbar^{-1}x[y]\) has \(bu=1\). Its Connes boundary \(Bu=\hbar^{-1}(1[x|y]-1[y|x])\) generates top Hochschild homology and survives in cyclic degree two. Thus the unit gives a nonzero ordinary cyclic degree-two class. Choose an algebraic cyclic two-cocycle \(\Phi\) on unnormalized chains with \(\Phi(1,1,1)=1\). Antisymmetrizing \(\Phi\) gives a closed Lie three-cochain on \(\mathfrak g\). For the chosen lift \(s:\mathfrak l\to\mathfrak g\), let \(P\) be its restriction to the three lifted inputs and put \(\beta(a)=\Phi(1,1,sa)\). The cyclic cocycle identity gives \(dP=\omega\wedge(\omega-d\beta)\). Hence \(H=P+\omega\wedge\beta\) satisfies \(dH=\omega\wedge\omega\). Contraction by \(H\) gives a bimodule homotopy for the two successive cap operations. At rank one, where the cap in degree two is an isomorphism, the component of the *outgoing cut* from degree four to two degree-two factors is zero. The higher Tor groups themselves are not determined by this identity.

This calculation places a real condition on a proposed physical junction. For *every* fixed spatial jet order \(L\), choose different odd \(d,e>L\). A trilinear primitive factoring through the order-\(L\) Taylor jet of each input would have zero differential on \(x^d,y^d,x^e,y^e\). Even after taking one bracket, two untouched inputs still have zero jets. Yet the marked square has value \(2c_dc_e\ne0\). The algebraic primitive can use arbitrarily high jets on polynomial inputs. An independent field theory would have to construct its two endpoint actions, preserve the cap and outgoing cut, and supply a contact homotopy in its own allowed space of distributions. Which jet orders and regularization it admits is a physical input.

theorems.title: Theorem: integral curved comparison
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: integral curved comparison.** For \(1\le N\le3\), there is a strictly unital \(R\)-linear \(A_\infty\) quasi-isomorphism
\[
K_N^{\mathrm{full}}\simeq_{A_\infty}e\Omega_S(C,w)e,
\]
without inverting or completing in \(\hbar\). Its derived zero fibre is formal, with algebra
\[
\left(\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N,y_1,\ldots,y_N]
\otimes\Lambda(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N)\right)^{S_N},
\qquad |\theta_i|=-1.
\]
The comparison uses ordered symbols and homotopy transfer over the polynomial parameter ring; the group-relative relations retain the permutation terms that ordinary symmetrization would lose. See [*The integral relative curved model*, main theorem](#ref-ch14-02).

theorems.title: Theorem: the exact chiral image
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: the exact chiral image.** For every \(N\ge1\), the framed relative complex has cohomology only in degree zero, in every conformal weight. Its algebra \(K_N\) is simple, with central charge \(-3N^2\) and a nondegenerate invariant form normalized on the vacuum. The natural map is injective and
\[
\alpha_N(K_N)=\ker(\chi^-_{(0)}:V_N\to V_N),
\qquad \chi^-=\phi\gamma.
\]
There is an odd global section \(\tau\) of conformal weight zero satisfying
\[
\chi^-_{(0)}\tau=N,
\qquad
V_N=\alpha_N(K_N)\oplus\tau_{(-1)}\alpha_N(K_N)
\]
as graded vector spaces. Thus the map is not surjective at any rank. The complementary factors are
\[
K_N=W_N\otimes\mathrm{Sb}\otimes\mathrm{SF},
\qquad
V_N=W_N\otimes\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc.
\]
Here \(\mathrm{Sb}\) is the trace symplectic-boson pair, \(\mathrm{SF}\) the symplectic-fermion algebra, and \(bc\) the fermionic pair of weights \((1,0)\). The total unframed relative cohomology is \(K_N\) for \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) and \(W_N\) for \(\mathfrak{sl}_N\), with ghost number matching framing fermion number. For \(N\ge2\), the traceless quadratic currents generate affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at level \(-(N^2-1)/2\); their zero modes give the Lie action used below. See [*Global sections on the Hilbert scheme*, Theorems A–B](#ref-ch14-06).

theorems.title: The order of separated surface collars
theorems.statement_excerpt: The order of two surface collars can detect the same sign. Put \(\tau=\hbar_{\mathrm b}/(4\pi^2)\). With the elementary right action \(Y=a\partial_X\), level-one unit surfaces, and incoming magnetic strength \(q_i=\tau/c_{\mathrm M}\) for Moyal parameter \([z,w]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\ne0\), the order-odd response to the test \(f(z)=z^2/2\) is \(\tau(j_2[f']-j_1[f'])/2\). Here \(j_i[f']=\operatorname{Res}f'(z)j^{(i)}(z)dz\). On \(|0\rangle_1\otimes j^{(2)}_{-1}|0\rangle_2\), the current in the second factor returns the vacuum and the first contributes zero. The reading is \(+\tau/2\) times the vacuum. Write \(S=J_1+J_2\) and \(Q=J_1J_2+\tfrac a2(\partial J_2-\partial J_1)\) for the first two elementary Weyl coefficients. The Miura stress tensor \(T=({:}S^2{:}-2Q)/(2k)\) gives the order-odd reading \(+a/2\) on the same marked vector at \(k=1\), fixing \(a=\tau\) at this order and in these markings. Integration by parts gives \(-a/2\) for the order-odd reading of \(Q\). At \(a=0,\ k=1\), the fourth pole of \(T(z)T(w)\) has vacuum coefficient one. An independently prepared magnetic flux must be compared with the stated incoming strength.

theorems.title: The one-loop cobar on finite root jets
theorems.statement_excerpt:
A Hall product can also be studied by asking what its Taylor coefficients do to one another. In the one-loop shuffle algebra the resulting comparison can be made over the polynomial ring \(R=\mathbb Q[\hbar]\). In charge \(m\) take \(A_m=R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]^{S_m}\), with \(A_0=R\). For this formula put the subobject in the first input. To multiply \(f\in A_p\) and \(g\in A_q\), sum over decompositions \(I\sqcup J=\{1,\ldots,p+q\}\), \(|I|=p\), the expressions
\[
 f(x_I)g(x_J)\prod_{i\in I,\,j\in J}
 \left(1+\frac{\hbar}{x_i-x_j}\right).
\]
The sum is a symmetric polynomial. For two singletons, write \(s(x,y)=(y,x)\) and \(u=x-y\). On an ordered two-variable input \(f\) the merge is \(f+sf+\hbar(f-sf)/u\). The last numerator is divisible by \(u\). In particular \(1*1=2\), \(x*1=x+y+\hbar\), and \(1*x=x+y-\hbar\). Thus exchange has a measurable effect even though the output is symmetric.

A finite root jet in \(W_m\) is an \(R\)-linear functional on \(A_m\) vanishing above some total root degree. For example \(J_i(f)=\partial_x^i f(0)\) in charge one. Form words on the positive-charge jets, each letter \(x(w)\) in cochain degree one. Transposing the Hall merge splits a letter into two and gives the differential of this cobar algebra \(\Omega(W)\). Let \(S_R\) be the zero-differential associative algebra on \(a_i\), \(i\ge0\), in degree and charge one. Its relations are the coefficients of
\[
 (z-w+\hbar)a(z)a(w)=(w-z+\hbar)a(w)a(z),
 \qquad a(z)=\sum_{i\ge0}a_i z^i.
\]
The augmented algebra map
\[
 F_R:\Omega(W)\longrightarrow S_R,\qquad
 x(J_i)\longmapsto i!\,a_i,\qquad
 x(w)\longmapsto0\quad\text{if \(w\) has charge greater than one}
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism in every charge. The derivative at the origin is \(i!\) times the coefficient of \(x^i\). For example the charge-two boundary of \(x(J_0^2)\) maps to \(2a_0^2+\hbar(a_1a_0-a_0a_1)\), the coefficient of \(z^1w^0\) in the exchange relation. The scalar unit maps to the scalar unit.

theorems.title: Theorem (ordinary K3 Hall comparison)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (ordinary K3 Hall comparison).** Choose the simultaneous cyclic minimal \(A_\infty\) model of the collection and a comparison with its Dolbeault category strictly unital over the quiver vertex-idempotent algebra \(\mathbb C^3\). There is a unique unital, charge-graded isomorphism
\[
\Theta:\mathcal C_\Pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_L
\]
sending the simple indicator at vertex \(i\) to \(1_{[L_i]}\). At every finite nilpotence bound it comes from an algebraic tensor family. Over reduced bases this family identifies reduced relative flag varieties, their subquotients, and all forgetting and regrouping maps. [Primitive recognition, Proposition “Regular families and the ordinary composition algebra”][ordinary-hall]

theorems.title: Scalar measurements recovering a compact first-order product
theorems.statement_excerpt:
How much information did those measurements lose? Fix the cup algebra, its grading, its unit, its pairing, all cap scalars, the whole operator \(\mu(F,-)\), and every trace \(\operatorname{Tr}\mu(D,-)\). Two commutative, cyclic first-order corrections differ by a symmetric cubic \(T\) on \(V\). Indeed, degrees and the unit force every other trilinear coefficient to vanish, and the first-order associator on three middle classes is \((T(a,b,c)-T(b,c,a))p=0\). The marked operator fixes \(T(F,-,-)=0\). The traces fix the contraction \(\tau_qT=0\), where \((\tau_qT)(a)=\sum_{ij}q^{ij}T(a,e_i,e_j)\) in any basis. Thus the space of differences is
\[
 \ker\!\left(\operatorname{Sym}^3 L\xrightarrow{\ \tau_q\ }L\right),
 \qquad L=\operatorname{Ann}(F)\subset V^* .
\]
Here \(L\) has dimension \(21\), and \(q^{-1}|_L\) has rank \(20\). Contraction is onto. For example, choose \(\ell\in L\) with nonzero square. Contracting \(\ell^3\) yields a nonzero multiple of \(\ell\), and contracting \(\operatorname{sym}(\ell^2m)\) for \(m\perp\ell\) yields a nonzero multiple of \(m\).
